sentence: This project tries to make freezing rat sperm and in vitro fertilization repeatable, so frozen rat models can be revived without intracytoplasmic sperm injection.
This project studies how chemical exposures that African American women face more often may lead to aggressive breast cancers.
This project tests whether losing mismatch repair gives intestinal stem cells an immediate growth or survival advantage that helps start cancer.
This project studies how drugs of abuse change the proteins in specific types of brain cells, to understand the molecular basis of drug addiction.
This project studies how the capsid of human immunodeficiency virus enters the nucleus of a host cell, using in vitro platforms and DNA nanotechnology.
This project builds an engineered surface that lets mucus move along it, for use on implanted medical devices.
This project provides analytical tools to researchers studying how cancer starts, so they can better understand cancer and develop ways to prevent it.
This project studies how two types of DNA in the cell communicate to keep mitochondria working, and how this breaks down in aging and dementia.
This project develops predictive algorithms based on smartphone measures to identify upcoming manic and depressive episodes early in Veterans with bipolar disorders.
This project studies how phase separation and other physical mechanisms organize and regulate heterochromatin, a mysterious part of our genomes.
This project builds a wearable device that analyzes odors from the skin, and develops algorithms that use its data to detect and monitor diseases.
This project builds a breast cancer scanner that combines positron emission tomography and x-ray tomosynthesis to measure how breast tumors respond to therapy.
This project studies how cells control their metabolism during viral infection, in both the latent and lytic stages.
This project studies how HIV comes to grow in macrophages and form a reservoir in the brain, using brain autopsy material.
This project studies the genetic, cellular and metabolic events behind lower urinary tract symptoms and urinary tract infections, and looks for ways to prevent them.
This project tests whether an AI tool that reads electrocardiograms can detect undiagnosed structural heart disease in emergency departments across diverse patients.
This project combines single-cell data with genetic data on disease to work out how noncoding regions of the genome regulate genes and shape disease.
This project studies which super enhancer elements are needed for gene expression during retinal development, and how they are conserved between mice and humans.
This project builds a way to measure how closely clinicians follow guidelines for airway disease in Veterans, using electronic health records and natural language processing.
This project studies how the posterior cerebellum affects heavy drinking in dependent mice and looks for the brain-wide targets of that effect.
